q: How much does SIDBI's 4E energy efficiency loan cover, and who qualifies?
title: SIDBI 4E loan: cover and eligibility
short: SIDBI's 4E loan funds energy efficiency projects up to ₹15 crore: 100 percent of the cost if you keep 25 percent as a fixed deposit, or up to 75 percent if you put in your own share. You need three years of operations with cash profit, and you must show the project cuts energy use or emissions.
audience: MSME owners planning an efficiency retrofit, and SIDBI or bank officers appraising one

sections.h: If you read the older terms
p: Many guides still describe 4E as 90 percent funding with a ₹10 lakh minimum after one year of operation and a detailed audit, or 100 percent against a 20 percent deposit. SIDBI's green finance page no longer shows those terms. Plan on the current ones below, and confirm them in your sanction letter.

ul: Fixed deposit route: 100 percent of the project, for loans up to ₹15 crore, with security of 25 percent kept as a fixed deposit.
Promoter contribution route: up to ₹15 crore, capped at 75 percent of project cost, so you pay at least a quarter yourself.
Either way: repayment over up to 84 months, with a moratorium of up to 12 months.
What it pays for: equipment and machinery, installation, minor civil works and commissioning of the efficiency measures.
An MSME in manufacturing or services that has run for at least three years, with cash profit in each of the last three financial years.
A project that establishes an energy efficiency gain or a cut in greenhouse gas emissions.
Compliance with SIDBI's Environment and Social Management Framework, so expect questions on pollution consents and worker safety.

sections.h: The condition that decides the file
p: The three-year record is a yes or no. The energy condition is where applications are won or lost. SIDBI needs to see a believable before and after: what the unit uses today, measured from bills, and what it will use once the new equipment runs. An auditor's report gives the expected saving; twelve months of bills and production records give the baseline that saving is measured against. If you make different products across the year, show energy per tonne or per piece, not just total units, so a busy month does not look like a failed project.

sections.h: What to put together before you apply
ol: Udyam registration and a clean repayment record with every lender.
Twelve months of electricity bills and fuel invoices, with production for the same months.
Supplier quotes for each machine, and the rated energy use of the old and new equipment.
An energy audit or technical note giving the expected yearly saving in kWh or fuel.
Your pollution control consents and safety records, for the environmental and social check.
A decision on which route you want: cash locked in a deposit, or cash spent on the project.

example.title: A ₹2 crore compressor and furnace retrofit
lines: Project cost: ₹2 crore, from supplier quotes
Fixed deposit route: loan ₹2 crore, with ₹50 lakh kept as a fixed deposit (25 percent)
Promoter route: loan up to ₹1.5 crore (75 percent), you pay ₹50 lakh into the project
Expected saving from the audit: 3,00,000 kWh a year
CO2 avoided: 3,00,000 kWh x 0.675 kg per kWh (CEA grid factor, FY 2025-26) = 2,02,500 kg, about 202 tonnes a year
Repayment: up to 84 months, with a moratorium of up to 12 months
example.note: Both routes ask for about ₹50 lakh of your own money here; the difference is whether it sits in a deposit you get back or goes into the machines. SIDBI's page does not say whether the 25 percent is measured on the loan or the project; at 100 percent funding the two are the same. The saving is the auditor's estimate until the bills after commissioning confirm it.

senseible: Senseible reads your last twelve months of electricity bills and fuel invoices into a monthly energy and CO2 baseline, the starting point for showing SIDBI the reduction 4E asks for, then compares the bills after commissioning against it. SIDBI decides the loan.
